title: Data Volume Estimation
description: Estimate storage, bandwidth, and throughput requirements to size your system correctly and justify architectural decisions with numbers.

data.text: Data volume estimation converts vague scale descriptions into concrete numbers. Interviewers expect you to calculate daily storage growth, read/write throughput, and bandwidth consumption. These numbers determine whether you need a distributed database, a CDN, or a message queue. Back-of-the-envelope calculations are not optional — they are the foundation of credible system design.

Start with user and behavior assumptions, then multiply to find total system load. Always state your assumptions explicitly so the interviewer can correct them. Round numbers to make arithmetic fast — 100 million users is easier to work with than 97,423,185. Divide large numbers into daily, hourly, and per-second figures to reveal peak load.

data.title: Estimation Steps:
items: Define user count and growth assumptions
Estimate actions per user per day
Convert to peak requests per second
Estimate storage per record and growth rate
Calculate bandwidth from payload size and request volume

data.text: Imagine designing a photo sharing app with 10 million daily active users. Each user uploads 2 photos per day, each photo is 2MB, and each user views 20 photos per day. Let us calculate the storage and bandwidth implications.

data.title: Storage and Bandwidth Calculation
data.content: Back-of-the-envelope estimation for a photo sharing app
data.code:
Assumptions:
- 10 million daily active users (DAU)
- 2 photos uploaded per user per day
- 2MB average photo size
- 20 photos viewed per user per day

Daily uploads = 10M users * 2 photos = 20M photos/day
Daily upload storage = 20M * 2MB = 40TB/day
Yearly upload storage = 40TB * 365 = ~14.6PB/year

Daily views = 10M users * 20 photos = 200M views/day
Peak view RPS = (200M views / 86,400 seconds) * 2 (peak factor) = ~4,600 RPS
Daily upload bandwidth = 20M * 2MB = 40TB/day
Upload RPS at peak = ~460 RPS

Storage strategy: Use object storage (S3) with CDN for reads. 14.6PB/year requires lifecycle policies for archival.

data.title: Always Show Your Work
data.text: Interviewers care more about your estimation process than the exact number. State assumptions, show formulas, and discuss how the result changes with different assumptions.

data.caption: Data volume estimation flow
data.definition:
graph TD
    A[User Assumptions] --> B[Behavior Per User]
    B --> C[Total Daily Operations]
    C --> D[Peak RPS]
    C --> E[Storage Growth]
    D --> F[Infrastructure Sizing]
    E --> F
    F --> G[Cost Estimate]
    F --> H[Architecture Decision]

data.text: The most common estimation mistakes are forgetting to account for growth rate, ignoring peak traffic multipliers, and underestimating metadata overhead. A 2MB photo is not the only data stored — user profiles, tags, comments, and indexes add 20 to 50 percent overhead. Always add a 2x to 5x peak multiplier to account for diurnal traffic patterns.

terms.definition: A quick, rough calculation using rounded numbers to estimate system scale.
Requests per second during the busiest period, typically 2-5x the average.
Rules for moving data between storage tiers based on age and access patterns.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Estimate storage, throughput, and bandwidth together
Always show your assumptions and calculations
Use peak multipliers to account for traffic spikes
data.takeaway: Data volume estimation turns a hand-wavy discussion into an evidence-based architecture discussion.
